a05_f00e: Good afternoon, Commander.
The President and the European Council are waiting for you.
Please stand by while I connect you.
Ah, Commander. I am glad you could join us.
The European Council and I have been discussing an aid package...
Only a possible one.
...a possible aid package for the United States.
The nuclear attack on Chicago seems to have given them something to consider.
Do not think we are indifferent to your situation, Mr. President.
But America is very far away from us.
Commander, for now we have agreed to send Special Agent Tanya on this mission,
in exchange for our allies providing troops and supplies to America.
Provided our conditions are met. I am prepared to give the order.
Could you all hold on for a moment? I am the one going on this mission.
We all need someone in command, Agent, do we not?
We have no time to train someone new, Mr. President.
If you want my help, you will send the Commander with me.
That is my condition.
Very well. Commander, if you agree...
Although it appears you have already been volunteered.
The Prime Minister will give you the details.
The objects in the second photograph are Soviet missile silos.
As you can see, Commander, they are close enough to threaten us.
I believe Romanov intends to intimidate us into staying out of the war.
Until this threat is removed, our forces will not be going anywhere.
Eliminate those missile silos, and we can bring this war closer to an end.
We are counting on you, Commander.
a05_p01e: It looks as though our infiltration was successful.
Our spy has entered the Soviet Battle Lab
and transmitted detailed information on the locations of their missile silos.
Commander, I am ready for some action.
Let us take out those silos and get ready to go home.
It is getting a little cold out here!
a05_p03e: Commander, watch out for Soviet attack dogs.
Soviet troops use attack dogs to detect spies.
